newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka devolution draft to be published in April.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka devolution draft to be published in April.

text.p: The final draft of the Sri Lankan government's devolution proposals aimed at ending the country's long-running ethnic war will be published in April, a senior government minister said on Friday.

Justice and Constitutional Affairs Minister Gamini Lakshman Peiris told a news conference the final draft of a new constitution would be made public in the first week of April, after local government elections are held on March 27.
"We thought it would be best to publish the final draft after the local government elections, when people have less politics on their minds," Peiris said.
The draft constitution, devolving wide-ranging powers to the regions and minority Tamils, is being discussed by a parliamentary select committee.

The government of President Chandrika Kumaratunga sees the proposed new constitution as offering an alternative to the war being fought by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) for a separate Tamil homeland in the island's north and east. The war is now in its 14th year.
The LTTE has ignored the devolution proposals, saying they will not accept anything short of independence.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war.
The draft constitution, the first version of which was unveiled in late 1995, must first be passed by a two-thirds majority in parliament and then approved in a national referendum.
It suggests turning Sri Lanka into a union of regions and making it a federal state in all but name.
Peiris, one of the architects of the devolution package, said two-thirds of the proposed new constitution was already finalised, except for the chapter on devolution of power.
The local elections are seen as the first test for Kumaratunga's People's Alliance government since it came to power in 1994.
Analysts say a victory for the alliance would be seen as a public endorsement of Kumaratunga's peace plan, which has been criticised by Sinhalese hardliners as rewarding the separatists.
